comment: T4 baseline (docs/TESTING.md). `load` and `context` in `taken` are the conditions of the MILLISECONDS rows — CPU load over 1-second samples before the run, and what invoked the binary. P2's phase-end measurement filled them from a controlled interleaved A/B against the P1 tree `46d939b`, six alternating pairs per scene. UI present is 12.13 ms (11.71–12.70), against P1's 21.36 ms (19.83–23.23): one UI draw and 48 890 instances make the complete 20 000-node scene 43% faster, but the roadmap's optimistic 2.0 ms prediction was not met. Sprite present is 1.77 ms (1.74–1.79), against P1's 2.11 ms (2.04–2.23), so guardrail 8 holds. GLYPH MODE AND THE WHITE-TEXEL CARD, 2026-09-22. The label's shaped quads are UI instances in glyph mode and the card binds the glyph atlas view, so the alternating card/label pair that held ui.draws at 20000 is one run now. Arithmetic for every moved row. ui.draws 20000 -> 1, P2's exit number met at its floor. ui.vertices 233340 -> 0: the labels were the last vertices and their quads are instances. ui.uiInstances 10000 -> 48890 = 10000 cards + 38890 glyph quads. ui.uploadBytes 8546880 -> 5280120, exactly 48890 x 108 B. ui.uploads 2 -> 1: no vertex stream left, one append. retainedNodes UNCHANGED at 10000 - the mesh stays on the node for the colour-pipeline fallback and this file still counts it. GLYPH LAYER, P3 step 3, 2026-09-24. sprites.atlasImages 1 -> 0: fontstash made its atlas image at setup, glyph pages are made by the first label, so a sprite-only scene makes none (guardrail 8). ui.atlasImages stays 1: one R8 1024x1024 page holds the bench's 40 distinct glyph tiles (10 digits x 4 x-variants). GLYPH COUNTERS AND THE TEXT BENCH, P3 step 8, 2026-09-24. New rows on every scene: glyphRasterizationsSteady counts rasterizations inside the 120 measured frames (the P3 exit: 0 in a steady state); glyphPages and glyphBytes are the R8 pages resident at the end; firstPaintRasterizations is the warm-up cost of frame 1 (ui 40 = 10 digits x 4 x-variants); sweepPeakPages and sweepRasterizations belong to the zoom sweep, which only the text scene runs. The text scene is 40 lines of an 80-character code line at 13 px, swept 0.5x -> 4x over 64 warm-up frames and settled at 1x: 3907 rasterizations through the sweep, never more than 2 pages (2 MiB) resident, 0 after it, and 2 760 glyph instances in one draw. Its present.ms baseline 0.29 is one standalone run, report-only, not an A/B. MEASURE CALL COST, P3.5, 2026-09-25. text.measureGlyphLookups counts the glyph-index lookups of one calcTextWidth of that 80-character line after warm-up, the call the Neon host's Yoga measure callback makes per text node: 80, one per glyph. It read 176 until the face's heights and decoration were measured once per face instead of on every call (95 ASCII glyphs for the extent, 1 ideograph). THE EDITOR SCENE, P4, 2026-09-26. One label holding 200 lines of 80 columns with three syntax runs per line, a selection over 12 rows and a caret: one draw, 13 214 UI instances (13 200 glyphs that are not spaces, 13 selection rows and the caret), 1 427 112 B uploaded per frame, 51 rasterizations on the first paint. Its present.ms baseline 0.58 is the median of five runs below 25% load in the window of P4's A/B (docs/VOID2D.md P4), report-only; the 6.12 first taken carried a TextLayout copy per selection row per frame (REVIEWS.md P4 B1). RETENTION, P5 step 7, 2026-09-28. A scene keeps its display list and its own GPU buffers between frames, emits again only the rows that changed, and writes a buffer only when its bytes changed, so the 120 measured frames of every bench scene, which change nothing, upload nothing. uploads 1 -> 0 and uploadBytes -> 0 on all four scenes. The full frame is still pinned: the new firstPaintUploadBytes row is frame 1's upload, ui 5 280 120 = 48 890 x 108 B, sprites 640 000 = 10 000 x 64 B, text 298 080 = 2 760 x 108 B, editor 1 427 112 = 13 214 x 108 B, the numbers uploadBytes carried per frame before. buffersAlive 3 -> 4 on every scene: the list's own instance buffer beside the frame buffer, the unit quad and the fullscreen quad; a scene with vertices or sprites and UI would hold one more per stream, still constant in the node count. THE CHANGE FLAG, P5 step 9, 2026-09-28. A scene reports whether a frame would draw anything new (Scene.isDirty, GPUI's is_dirty gating its frame callback), and a host presents only then. idleDirty is that flag read after the 120 measured frames, which change nothing: 0 on every scene, so a host following the contract draws and uploads nothing while the scene is still.

taken.renderer: the unified UI pipeline: cards and glyph quads are instances; one run, one draw
taken.load: 11.77% CPU mean over five 1 s samples before the run
taken.context: interleaved A/B vs 46d939b, six alternating pairs per scene
